key_insight: SynCo co-trains a task synthesizer and a solver so the training data evolves with model ability, reducing the mismatch that makes static synthetic datasets become either too easy or too hard.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning systems, this suggests a practical path to continual self-improvement by jointly adapting data generation and policy learning instead of freezing one side of the loop.
method: Multi-agent reinforcement learning jointly updates a Synthesizer and a Reasoner.
The Synthesizer creates tasks conditioned on the Reasoner’s evolving capability state.
Rollout outcomes provide correctness, quality, reliability, and teachability rewards for both agents.
evidence_signal: The paper reports strong gains across eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with most improvements coming from previously unsolved problems.
watch_item: The approach adds training complexity and may depend on stable reward design; if rewards are poorly calibrated, task synthesis can drift toward overly easy or noisy problems.
paper_title: SynCo: Data Synthesis Co-Training for Self-Evolving LLMs via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
